## In short {#summary}

AI assistants are welcome during the workshop, with three exceptions: your
first prediction, the Kahoot quizzes, and the entry and exit checks are yours
alone. Whatever an assistant tells you, run the code and look at the shape:
the notebook's own check decides, not the assistant.

## Using AI during the workshop {#during-the-workshop}

You may use any AI assistant, including Gemini inside Colab, to explain an
error message, a NumPy function or a term, and to review code you have
already written. Try each exercise yourself first, the same way you try it
before opening its folded solution, and then ask for help.

### Three things are yours alone {#yours-alone}

- **Your first prediction.** Sections open on a predict-first question, and
  some on a *Myth or fact?* claim. Make your own guess before you run
  anything or ask anyone. A wrong guess you made yourself teaches you more
  than a right one you were given.
- **The Kahoot quizzes.** Play them on your own, from memory.
- **The entry and exit checks.** They measure what you understand, so the
  instructors can see where the room is. An assistant's answer tells them
  nothing about that.

### Check what it tells you {#check}

An assistant can sound sure and still be wrong, and it is wrong most often
about what this workshop is about: which axis is which, and what shape comes
out. Before you trust an answer:

- run it, and print `.shape`;
- compare it with the notebook's expected result and with the
  [handbook](tensors_workshop_plan_with_quizzes.md);
- if the two disagree, trust the notebook's check and ask in
  [Discord]({{< var community.discord >}}).

The [worked mistakes](worked-mistakes.md) are good practice: each one is code
that runs, prints something plausible, and is wrong.

### Say when it helped {#disclose}

When your group posts its three-line share-back in Discord, or you share work
from the workshop anywhere else, say whether an AI assistant helped, and how.
This page does the same for the materials.

### Keep private data out {#privacy}

The workshop's datasets are public, so pasting them into an assistant is
fine. Do not paste anything that is not yours to share: data from your job,
other people's personal information, passwords or API keys.

## How AI was used to make this workshop {#how-we-used-ai}

- **Code and site.** The notebooks, the interactive widgets, this site and
  the scripts that build and check them were written with AI coding
  assistants (Claude, from Anthropic), working under the instructors'
  direction. Most commits in the [repository]({{< var repo.url >}}) name an
  AI co-author.
- **The Spanish handbook** is a machine translation of the English one, which
  remains the source of truth.
- **The [companion](companion.qmd)'s** summaries, audio, videos and
  self-checks were generated with NotebookLM and have not been checked by a
  person.
- **What is checked automatically.** Every change to the site reruns each
  notebook's core route against the real datasets and checks the numbers it
  prints. Nothing checks prose that way, in either language.
- **Who is responsible.** The instructors chose what is taught and in what
  order, and they are responsible for every error, whoever or whatever wrote
  it first. If you find one, say so in
  [Discord]({{< var community.discord >}}) or write to
  [{{< var event.contact >}}](mailto:{{< var event.contact >}}).
